newsitem.title: UK: LIFFE white sugar holds most fund-inspired gains.
newsitem.headline: LIFFE white sugar holds most fund-inspired gains.

text.p: White sugar futures held onto most of the gains notched up during the morning's fund-led buying spree as the nearby August contract motored higher and towards fresh upside targets.
Earlier, a renewed bout of fund buying pushed August over $330 a tonne, building on the rally seen in late activity on Monday.
"All the buying is coming into the August," said one trader. "If suddenly other people start coming out and buying sugar at these levels, then you have to say the levels are justified."
By 1530 GMT all positions were firmer and hovering close to intraday highs. August stood up $2.20 at $330.00 having moved in a wide $3.20 ranges.
October was up $2.00 at $320.50 and volume reached a hefty 3,598 lots, dominated by August. Market sources cited a sprinkling of crossed and against actuals trades which boosted the total volume.

The funds had been lured by August's good liquidity and strong technical picture, they said, noting that the rally had also pushed August into overbought territory -- opening up the possibility of a technical correction.
Analysts pegged August's next resistance points at $333.50, followed by $341.00.
Traders also mentioned a fair amount of Brazilian pricing in the London market, as well in New York.
Russian physical demand is still a talking point but details of actual purchases have been scarce due to the small amounts of white sugar reported to be trickling into Baltic and Black Sea ports.
"If Russia keeps buying, the chances are August could still be fairly tight and a lot of the pricing that's been put in there may end up having to be put back," the trader said.
Trading in Paris was also dominated by August, which was up $2.40 at $329.00. October was untraded and Matif volume totalled 494 lots.
